notes.1: SOURCE: Agilent 33250A 80 MHz Waveform Generator User's Guide, publication number 33250-90002, Edition 2, March 2003, Chapter 8 "Specifications", printed pp. 319-323 (PDF pp. 321-324; row "page" = PDF page = printed page + 1). Read from rendered page images, each block twice; the readings agree. Built by specs/build_33250a_standard.py.
notes.2: PERIOD AND CONFIDENCE: the manual states the frequency accuracy for "1 year" and a Calibration Interval of 1 year; every figure on this sheet is stored under "1 yr" (default period). The manual states NO confidence level and no k: "not specified", stored with no level (divisor 2, laboratory convention, as the 8563E / 3458A / T-10A sheets). The manual also says nothing on whether the figures are warranted limits or typical values except where it writes "typical" (phase noise, impedance), which is NOT stored.
notes.3: CONDITIONS: output characteristics are into 50 ohm (the open-circuit amplitude range is 20 mVpp to 20 Vpp, printed footnote 2); amplitude and offset accuracy at 1 kHz, above 10 mVpp, Autorange ON (printed p. 321). Warm-up time 1 hour (general specifications, printed p. 323). Printed footnote 1 of Output Characteristics: add 1/10th of the output amplitude AND offset specification per degC for operation outside 18 degC to 28 degC (1-year specification); NOT applied to any stored row (a lab at 18 - 28 degC needs nothing).
notes.4: FREQUENCY (printed p. 320): "Accuracy (1 year): 2 ppm, 18 degC to 28 degC; 3 ppm, 0 degC to 55 degC". Stored: 2 ppm of the setting (+/-(2 ppm I.V.)), range 1 uHz to 80 MHz (sine and square). The 3 ppm figure for 0 - 55 degC is NOT stored as a row (a plain lookup takes the larger limit of every matching row and would always return 3 ppm). Waveform limits: sine and square 1 uHz - 80 MHz, ramp 1 uHz - 1 MHz, pulse 500 uHz - 50 MHz, arb 1 uHz - 25 MHz (printed p. 320); the 80 MHz row is the maximum. Resolution 1 uHz, pulse 5 digits (not stored). The manual prints NO separate ageing or stability figure for the 10 MHz time base: the 2 ppm one-year accuracy is the only time-base specification.
notes.5: AMPLITUDE (printed p. 321): range 10 mVpp to 10 Vpp into 50 ohm. Accuracy (at 1 kHz, >10 mVpp, Autorange On): +/-(1 % of setting + 1 mVpp). Stored in the manual's own unit (Vpp), no conversion to Vrms. "Setting" is the amplitude setting in Vpp (units Vpp, Vrms, dBm, High / Low level are all selectable; the spec is printed in Vpp). Resolution 0.1 mV or 4 digits (not stored).
notes.6: FLATNESS (printed p. 321): sinewave relative to 1 kHz, Autorange On: below 10 MHz +/-1 % (0.1 dB), 10 MHz to 50 MHz +/-2 % (0.2 dB), 50 MHz to 80 MHz +/-5 % (0.4 dB). Printed footnote 3: dB rounded to 1 digit; the instrument adheres to the "%" specification (so the % figures are stored). The lower edge of "<10 MHz" is not printed: 1 uHz (the lowest sine frequency) is used.
notes.7: DERIVED ROWS (not printed as such): the "Voltage, AC [Sinewave into 50 Ohm, Vpp]" rows for frequency bands are the 1 kHz accuracy (1 % + 1 mVpp) PLUS the printed flatness of the band (arithmetic worst-case sum: 2 %, 3 %, 6 % + 1 mVpp); the manual does not say how the two combine. The 1 kHz row is the printed accuracy alone; the bands next to it start / stop 1 uHz away (999.999999 Hz, 1000.000001 Hz, the frequency resolution) so that exactly 1 kHz finds only the printed row. A frequency exactly on 10 MHz or 50 MHz takes the worse (higher) row (NOTES.md "Frequency band edges").
notes.8: OFFSET (printed p. 321): range +/-5 V peak (ac + dc) into 50 ohm. Accuracy: 1 % of setting + 2 mV + 0.5 % of amplitude. The amplitude term depends on the waveform amplitude, which the schema cannot hold per point: function "[Offset, DC Volts waveform, 50 Ohm]" assumes amplitude 0 (+/-(1 % I.V. + 2 mV)); function "[Offset under a waveform, 50 Ohm]" bounds the term at the 10 Vpp maximum (0.5 % x 10 Vpp = 50 mV, stored as 0.5 % F.S., Full Scale = 10 Vpp). "Amplitude" is taken as the Vpp setting (UNVERIFIED). The plain DCV lookup returns the larger (waveform) row; ask for variant "DC Volts" for the amplitude-0 case.
notes.9: SQUARE WAVE (printed p. 320): rise / fall time < 8 ns (printed footnote 4: edge time is decreased at higher frequency), overshoot < 5 %, asymmetry 1 % of period + 1 ns, jitter (rms) below 2 MHz 0.01 % + 525 ps and 2 MHz and above 0.1 % + 75 ps; duty cycle 20.0 % to 80.0 % (to 25 MHz), 40.0 % to 60.0 % (25 - 50 MHz), 50.0 % fixed (50 - 80 MHz). "%" is taken as per cent of the PERIOD (the manual says "1% of period" for asymmetry and nothing for the jitter terms: ASSUMED the same). Rise time is stored as a "<=" limit (the manual prints "<").
notes.10: JITTER IS rms: the figures are a standard deviation (one sigma), not a bound; they are stored as +/-(...) terms so the lookup returns the printed magnitude, but a budget that divides a sheet value by the coverage divisor (2) would halve a quantity that is already a standard deviation. Nothing selects the TIME rows of this sheet today.
notes.11: PULSE (printed p. 320): period 20.00 ns to 2000.0 s, pulse width 8.0 ns to 1999.9 s, variable edge time 5.00 ns to 1.00 ms, overshoot < 5 %, jitter (rms) 100 ppm + 50 ps. The manual prints NO accuracy for pulse width, period or edge time (only ranges and resolution digits): none is stored. ARB (printed p. 320): minimum edge time < 10 ns, linearity < 0.1 % of peak output, settling time < 50 ns to 0.5 % of final value, jitter (rms) 30 ppm + 2.5 ns. RAMP: linearity < 0.1 % of peak output, symmetry 0.0 % to 100.0 %.
notes.12: SPECTRAL PURITY (printed p. 320), sine, kind OTHER (limits in dBc, "<=" rows): harmonic distortion < 3 Vpp / > 3 Vpp: DC - 1 MHz -60 / -55 dBc, 1 - 5 MHz -57 / -45 dBc, 5 - 80 MHz -37 / -30 dBc (footnote 2: low amplitudes limited by a -70 dBm floor); total harmonic distortion DC to 20 kHz < 0.2 % + 0.1 mVrms; spurious (non-harmonic) DC - 1 MHz -60 dBc, 1 - 20 MHz -50 dBc, 20 - 80 MHz -50 dBc + 6 dBc/octave (footnote 3: limited by a -75 dBm floor). The 6 dBc/octave slope is only in the row text; the stored number is -50 dBc. "3 Vpp" itself sits in both columns of the printed table (< 3 / > 3): stored as 0 - 3 Vpp and 3 - 10 Vpp.
notes.13: TYPICAL ONLY, NOT STORED: phase noise (30 kHz band) < -65 dBc at 10 MHz and < -47 dBc at 80 MHz (printed "typical"); waveform output impedance 50 ohm typical. Other printed items not stored: arbitrary waveform length / sample rate / memory, configuration and arb download times, trigger input / output, burst, sweep, modulation, phase offset (range -360 deg to +360 deg, resolution 0.001 deg; no accuracy printed), clock reference (external lock 10 MHz +/- 35 kHz; internal reference output 10 MHz, 632 mVpp), sync output, general specifications.

problems.what: Source: Agilent 33250A User's Guide, 33250-90002 Edition 2 (March 2003), Chapter 8, printed pp. 319-323. Row 'page' fields are PDF page numbers (printed page + 1). Read from rendered images, each block twice.
Period "1 yr" (the manual states the accuracy for 1 year and a 1 year calibration interval). No confidence level / k is printed: stored with no level, divisor 2 (laboratory convention). ASSUMED.

The manual prints no separate ageing / stability figure for the 10 MHz time base; only "Accuracy (1 year) 2 ppm, 18 - 28 degC; 3 ppm, 0 - 55 degC". The 3 ppm figure is in the notes only; the lab temperature range is assumed to be 18 - 28 degC.

DERIVED: the frequency-band rows add the printed flatness to the printed 1 kHz accuracy (arithmetic sum, 2 % / 3 % / 6 % + 1 mVpp); the manual does not print the combination. The 1 kHz row is the printed figure.

Unit Vpp as printed: the rows are EXCLUDED from a plain AC volts lookup (specmanager.DEFAULT_VARIANT excludes "vpp", a value in V rms would match the wrong band); ask for variant "Vpp". ">10 mVpp" is printed for the accuracy; the 10 mVpp lower edge is stored.
Band edges 999.999999 Hz and 1000.000001 Hz (1 uHz either side of 1 kHz) keep exactly 1 kHz on the printed row; the lower edge of "<10 MHz" is not printed (1 uHz assumed).

problems.where: Voltage, DC [Offset under a waveform, 50 Ohm]
problems.what: The "0.5 % of amplitude" term depends on the waveform amplitude, which the sheet cannot hold per point: bounded at the 10 Vpp maximum (50 mV). UNVERIFIED that "amplitude" means the Vpp setting. A plain DCV lookup returns this larger row.

problems.where: Voltage, DC [Offset, DC Volts waveform, 50 Ohm]
problems.what: ASSUMED: the DC Volts waveform has amplitude 0, so the amplitude term is 0. The manual does not say so.

Jitter (rms) rows are one-sigma standard deviations stored as +/-(...) magnitudes; "%" of the period is ASSUMED for the jitter terms (the manual says "of period" only for asymmetry). A budget dividing by the divisor would halve an already-standard figure.

The manual prints NO accuracy for pulse width, period, edge time or duty cycle (ranges and resolution digits only): none stored (see "limits"). Owner to say whether a pulse-width accuracy is wanted from the service guide.
Printed "< 8 ns" (footnote 4: decreased at higher frequency), stored as "<=" 8 ns, value range 0 (the 5522A rise-time convention).

Kind OTHER, "<=" limits in dBc (the 8563E convention); the 20 - 80 MHz spurious slope "+ 6 dBc/octave" is in the text only; THD stored as 0.2 % + 0.1 mV (rms). Phase noise is "typical" in the manual and is NOT stored.

NOT STORED (printed, no accuracy or typical only): resolution (frequency 1 uHz, pulse 5 digits; amplitude 0.1 mV or 4 digits), phase offset, amplitude / frequency / period / pulse width / edge time ranges, phase noise (typical), impedance (50 ohm typical), trigger, burst, sweep, modulation, reference clock, sync, configuration and download times, general specifications (see notes 11 and 13).
Confidence level is not specified on the sheet; set the coverage divisor in the manager before relying on this standard.
